newsitem.title: USA: LA Cty lawyer writes PSA on escrow data request.
newsitem.headline: LA Cty lawyer writes PSA on escrow data request.

text.p: A key lawyer for a Los Angeles County authority said he has asked his client to consider turning over key underlying data from a recent controversial "yield burning" study to Wall Street.

John Phillips, a partner with Phillips & Cohen in Washington, D.C., told Reuters TV that he just sent a letter to PSA's Bond Market Trade Association saying that the firm has referred PSA's request for more data to its client, the Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority.
"I just sent a letter to PSA, saying we've referred .. their request for turning over the data ... to our client. We're certainly willing to do that," Phillips said.

But he signaled that the county wants detailed data from bond dealers in return. Specifically, the county wants data on a transaction-by-transaction basis from dealers who did escrow transactions, he said.
"We'd like to work with PSA to get access to some of the data that they possess and their members possess," Phillips said. "We all want to get accurate information."
PSA President Heather Ruth had said earlier in the Reuters broadcast that individual bond dealers oppose handing over detailed data for "due process" reasons.
"PSA doesn't have data regarding (each) transaction," Ruth said. "Our members do."

But because some dealers are under federal agency probes of possible yield burning, they "are not in a position to release data," Ruth said. Such dealers are "protecting their own rights to due process," Ruth said.
Phillips said, to date, the county has given background data from its study to the IRS, but not to the public.
Yield burning refers to allegations that bond underwriteres overcharge issuers for U.S. Treasury securities purchased in the open market and used in bond refinancing transactions.
